metadata.prompt_summary: Locked Sunday grilled chicken. Cravings: soup dumplings, spring rolls, green goddess salad, chicken corn street tacos, leftover corned beef, lemon ricotta pancakes. Favorites: Babo Pasta, shrimp jambalaya. No cabbage (Elsie). Weather: hot Sunday, rainy Monday, cold/sunny midweek, parents night out Friday, cold Saturday.

candidates.name: Grilled Chicken Thighs with Tabbouleh, Hummus & Turmeric Rice
candidates.description: Bone-in chicken thighs grilled over high heat until charred and juicy, served alongside bright parsley-heavy tabbouleh, creamy homemade hummus, and fragrant turmeric-tinted basmati rice. A complete mezze plate on one dish.
candidates.why: LOCKED for Sunday. 84°F grilling weather makes this ideal. Middle Eastern cuisine fulfills House Rule. Three-component plate ensures Elsie finds something she likes.

candidates.name: Corned Beef Hash with Fried Eggs & Toast
candidates.description: Crispy-edged cubes of leftover corned beef and golden potatoes, pan-fried in a cast-iron skillet until deeply caramelized, topped with runny fried eggs. The kind of dinner that turns leftovers into the best meal of the week.
candidates.why: Uses leftover corned beef (user craving). Only 25 min — perfect for Monday's busy schedule (meetings 3-8 PM). Rainy 66°F-36°F weather calls for skillet comfort food. Elsie loves fried eggs and crispy potatoes.

candidates.name: One-Pot Shrimp & Andouille Jambalaya
candidates.description: A soul-warming one-pot wonder: smoky andouille sausage, plump Gulf shrimp, and long-grain rice simmered with the Cajun holy trinity, tomatoes, and a heavy hand of Cajun spice. Shrimp goes in at the last minute so it stays tender.
candidates.why: Family favorite request — they specifically want to make this. One-pot makes it weeknight-friendly. Warming and hearty for Tuesday's cold 49°F sunny weather. Two proteins (shrimp + sausage) add depth.

candidates.name: Babo Pasta (Homemade Spinach Pasta with Egg Yolks)
candidates.description: The family's weekly ritual: silky spinach-green pasta made from scratch with '00' flour, fresh spinach, and a generous helping of egg yolks for that impossibly rich, golden color and tender bite. Tossed simply with brown butter and Parmigiano-Reggiano.
candidates.source_name: Family Recipe / Cooking with Mamma C
candidates.why: Weekly staple — Babo Pasta is a non-negotiable family tradition. Italian cuisine fulfills House Rule. The meditative rolling process fits a Wednesday evening nicely.

candidates.name: Chicken & Charred Corn Street Tacos with Elote Crema
candidates.description: Cumin-lime marinated chicken thighs, grilled and sliced, piled onto warm corn tortillas with fire-charred corn, cotija crumble, and a smoky chipotle-lime crema. Elote vibes in taco form — street food that makes your kitchen smell like a Mexico City mercado.
candidates.why: Direct user craving. Thursday's 67°F sunny spring day is perfect taco weather. Different from the American Tacos made two weeks ago — this is elote-forward Mexican street style. Elsie loves tacos.

candidates.name: Lemon Ricotta Pancakes with Warm Berry Compote
candidates.description: Cloud-light pancakes made with whole-milk ricotta and bright lemon zest, with whipped egg whites folded in for a soufflé-like rise. Served with a quick warm blueberry-strawberry compote and real maple syrup. Breakfast-for-dinner at its finest.
candidates.why: User craving. Perfect for Friday when Elsie eats separately before YAT — pancakes are her kind of comfort food and dead simple. Quick enough that parents can still get out the door for date night.

candidates.name: Soup Dumplings (Xiao Long Bao)
candidates.description: The crown jewel of dumpling making: delicate thin-skinned dumplings filled with seasoned pork and a burst of rich, gelatinous broth that melts into soup when steamed. A Saturday project that rewards patience with pure magic. Served with black vinegar and ginger strips.
candidates.why: User's top craving — soup dumplings/Asian things. Saturday's 46°F cold makes this the perfect cozy ambitious project. Shanghainese cuisine adds diversity. Elsie will love the 'magic soup inside' factor. Gelatin stock can be made Friday night.

candidates.name: Fresh Vietnamese Spring Rolls with Peanut Dipping Sauce
candidates.description: Translucent rice paper wrapped around vermicelli noodles, poached shrimp, crisp lettuce, julienned carrots, cucumber, and a bouquet of fresh herbs (mint, Thai basil, cilantro). Served with a rich peanut-hoisin dipping sauce. Cool, crunchy, and impossibly fresh.
candidates.why: User craving for spring rolls and Asian things. Great DIY dinner — set up a rolling station and let everyone build their own. No cooking required beyond boiling shrimp/noodles. Adds Vietnamese cuisine diversity.

candidates.name: Shakshuka with Crusty Sourdough
candidates.description: Eggs poached in a spiced, garlicky tomato-pepper sauce — cumin, paprika, and a touch of harissa give it warmth without overwhelming heat. Finished with crumbled feta and fresh herbs, scooped up with thick slices of crusty sourdough bread.
candidates.why: Vegetarian option that's hearty enough for dinner. One-skillet, 30-minute meal. Middle Eastern/North African origin adds diversity and fulfills House Rule. Elsie likes eggs and bread-dipping. Perfect comfort food for a cold evening.

candidates.name: Spring Pea & Asparagus Risotto with Lemon and Mint
candidates.description: Creamy Arborio rice slowly stirred with white wine and vegetable stock, finished with blanched spring peas, roasted asparagus tips, a shower of Parmigiano, bright lemon zest, and torn mint. Seasonal spring ingredients at their absolute best.
candidates.why: Vegetarian dinner that celebrates early spring East Coast produce (asparagus and peas arriving at markets in late March). Second Italian dish provides variety within a beloved cuisine. Creamy texture appeals to Elsie.

candidates.name: Crispy Tofu Pad See Ew
candidates.description: Wide rice noodles stir-fried in a scorching hot wok with crispy pressed tofu, Chinese broccoli (or regular broccoli), egg, and a savory-sweet sauce of soy, oyster sauce, and a touch of vinegar. Smoky, chewy, and deeply savory — Thai street food at home.
candidates.why: Additional vegetarian Asian option (feeds the spring rolls/Asian craving). Super fast — 25 minutes. Thai cuisine adds another dimension of diversity. Noodles are always a hit with Elsie.

candidates.name: Spring Vegetable Frittata with Goat Cheese & Herbs
candidates.description: A golden, puffed frittata loaded with sautéed spring vegetables — asparagus, peas, leeks, and fresh herbs — studded with tangy goat cheese. Starts on the stovetop, finishes under the broiler. Elegant enough for company, easy enough for Tuesday.
candidates.why: Additional vegetarian option that showcases March seasonal produce. Quick one-pan meal. Breakfast-for-dinner adjacent but more sophisticated. The goat cheese adds a tangy richness that elevates simple eggs.

candidates.name: Reuben Egg Rolls with Russian Dressing
candidates.description: All the glory of a Reuben sandwich — corned beef, Swiss cheese, and tangy sauerkraut — rolled up in a crispy egg roll wrapper and fried until shattering-crisp. Served with homemade Russian dressing for dipping. The best use of leftover corned beef that isn't a sandwich.
candidates.why: Creative use of leftover corned beef. Connects to the Asian theme (egg roll format). NOTE: Contains sauerkraut (fermented cabbage) — if serving to Elsie, swap sauerkraut for extra Swiss cheese or pickles.

candidates.name: Whipped Spring Pea & Ricotta Crostini with Mint
candidates.description: Bright green spring peas and creamy ricotta whipped together with lemon zest, garlic, and fresh mint, spooned onto golden toasted baguette rounds. Finished with a drizzle of good olive oil and flaky salt. Spring on a crouton.
candidates.why: Seasonal spring appetizer that connects to the ricotta theme (lemon ricotta pancakes). Quick 15-min prep. The bright green color and mild, sweet flavor appeal to kids and adults alike.

candidates.name: Green Goddess Salad with Avocado, Crispy Chickpeas & Seeds
candidates.description: A generous tossed salad of crisp romaine, shaved cucumber, green onions, and ripe avocado, coated in a vibrant herb-packed Green Goddess dressing. Topped with spiced crispy roasted chickpeas and toasted pumpkin seeds for protein and crunch.
candidates.dressing: Green Goddess dressing: fresh basil, fresh parsley, fresh chives, tarragon, 1 small garlic clove, 2 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp rice vinegar, 1/4 cup Greek yogurt, 1/4 cup extra-virgin olive oil, 1 tbsp white miso paste, salt, black pepper. Blend until smooth and vivid green.
candidates.flavor_rationale: The creamy herb dressing coats every leaf with bright, almost grassy freshness, while the miso adds a subtle umami backbone that makes you keep eating. Crispy chickpeas bring satisfying crunch and protein, turning a side salad into a full meal. The avocado adds richness that rounds out the acidity from lemon and vinegar.
candidates.seasonal_note: Late March sees the first spring herbs arriving at East Coast markets — chives, parsley, and tarragon are at their most vibrant. Avocados are in peak season year-round. Chickpeas bridge the gap before summer proteins arrive.
candidates.why: Direct user craving for Green Goddess salad. Hearty enough for a standalone dinner with the crispy chickpeas and avocado. The herb-forward dressing is the star — this is the salad people ask for the recipe.

candidates.name: Fattoush with Za'atar Croutons & Sumac Vinaigrette
candidates.description: An artfully arranged composed plate: torn pita crisped with za'atar and olive oil, arranged over a bed of little gem lettuce, sliced radishes, cherry tomatoes, Persian cucumbers, and fresh herbs. Drizzled with a bright sumac-lemon vinaigrette. Each component placed intentionally for visual impact.
candidates.dressing: Sumac vinaigrette: 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, 2 tbsp fresh lemon juice, 1 tsp ground sumac, 1 small minced garlic clove, 1 tsp pomegranate molasses, pinch of Aleppo pepper, salt to taste. Whisk until emulsified.
candidates.flavor_rationale: Sumac's tart, almost berry-like acidity is the backbone — it brightens every vegetable it touches. The pomegranate molasses adds a dark, sweet-sour depth that makes the dressing complex and addictive. Za'atar croutons bring herbal crunch that echoes the fresh herbs throughout. This is the principle of layering similar flavors in different textures.
candidates.seasonal_note: Radishes are among the first spring vegetables at East Coast markets. Little gem lettuce is hardy enough to be available in late March. This salad bridges winter's heartiness with spring's brightness.
candidates.why: Composed dinner salad with stunning visual presentation. Middle Eastern origin complements the grilled chicken Sunday dinner beautifully. The za'atar pita croutons make it substantial and fun for Elsie to eat.

candidates.name: Shaved Carrot & Radish Salad with Sesame-Ginger Dressing
candidates.description: Ribbons of carrot and thinly sliced watermelon radish, tossed with a nutty sesame-ginger dressing and sprinkled with toasted sesame seeds and sliced scallions. Light, crunchy, and clean — the perfect counterpoint to rich Asian mains.
candidates.dressing: Sesame-ginger dressing: 2 tbsp toasted sesame oil, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp freshly grated ginger, 1 tsp honey, 1 tsp lime juice, pinch of red pepper flakes. Whisk together.
candidates.flavor_rationale: The warm nuttiness of sesame oil meets the bright snap of rice vinegar and ginger, creating a dressing that enhances without overpowering the natural sweetness of the carrots. The radish adds a peppery bite that keeps the palate awake. Soy sauce brings umami depth. This is the Asian principle of balancing sweet, salty, sour, and aromatic in every bite.
candidates.seasonal_note: Carrots are a year-round East Coast staple, and watermelon radishes (with their stunning pink interior) are available through early spring at farmers' markets. This salad celebrates root vegetables at their late-winter/early-spring peak.
candidates.why: Side salad designed to pair with the Asian mains (soup dumplings, spring rolls, pad see ew). Japanese-inspired flavors add cuisine diversity to the salad lineup. Beautiful color from the watermelon radish.

candidates.name: Spring Arugula Salad with Strawberries, Pecans & Goat Cheese
candidates.description: Peppery arugula tossed with sliced early-season strawberries, candied pecans, and crumbles of tangy chèvre. A classic French-inspired combination where every element has a clear role: bitter, sweet, crunchy, creamy.
candidates.dressing: Strawberry-balsamic vinaigrette: 2 ripe strawberries (mashed), 2 tbsp aged balsamic vinegar, 1 tsp Dijon mustard, 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil, 1 tsp honey, pinch of salt and cracked black pepper. Whisk until slightly thickened.
candidates.flavor_rationale: The peppery bite of arugula is softened by sweet strawberries and balanced by the tangy acidity of balsamic and goat cheese. Candied pecans provide a butter-sweet crunch that contrasts the soft greens. The strawberry in the vinaigrette creates an echo effect — the same ingredient appearing in two forms — which gives the salad a sense of intentional coherence.
candidates.seasonal_note: Florida strawberries are at peak season in March and widely available on the East Coast. Arugula is one of the first spring greens. Early pecans from fall harvest store well through spring. This salad bridges the gap between winter and the first real taste of spring produce.
candidates.why: A different flavor profile from the other salads — French-inspired, fruit-forward, and elegant. Pairs beautifully with the Italian dishes (Babo pasta, risotto) and lighter mains. Kids love the sweet strawberry element.

candidates.name: Sazerac
candidates.description: The official cocktail of New Orleans: rye whiskey stirred with a sugar cube and Peychaud's bitters, served in an absinthe-rinsed rocks glass with a lemon peel twist. Spirit-forward, aromatic, and deeply satisfying.
candidates.pairing_note: The natural partner for jambalaya night. The rye's spice mirrors the Cajun seasoning, while the absinthe's anise adds an aromatic layer that lifts the rich, smoky flavors of andouille. A proper New Orleans evening at home.
candidates.why: Classic NOLA cocktail that creates a complete Cajun/Creole dinner experience alongside the jambalaya. Spirit-forward enough to stand up to bold flavors.

candidates.name: New Zealand Sauvignon Blanc (Cloudy Bay or Oyster Bay)
candidates.description: Crisp, zesty, and herbaceous with notes of grapefruit, passion fruit, and freshly cut grass. NZ Sauvignon Blanc is the Swiss Army knife of food wines — it cuts through richness and complements bright, herby dishes alike.
candidates.pairing_note: Pairs with nearly everything this week: the herbs in spring rolls, the lemon in ricotta pancakes, the brightness of tabbouleh, and the peanut sauce dipping. Its high acidity and citrus character refresh the palate between bites of rich or spicy food. Buy two bottles.
candidates.why: Versatile weekly wine that works across multiple cuisines. Affordable ($12-18) and widely available. The herbaceous notes echo the fresh herbs throughout the menu.

candidates.name: Sparkling Thyme Lemonade
candidates.description: A non-alcoholic sparkler made with fresh-squeezed lemon juice, thyme-infused simple syrup, and topped with cold sparkling water. Bright, herbal, and incredibly refreshing — the grown-up lemonade Elsie will love too.
candidates.pairing_note: The family-friendly option that pairs across the entire week. The thyme adds an herbal sophistication that elevates it beyond basic lemonade, while the bubbles make it feel festive. Especially lovely with the Middle Eastern dishes and the lighter spring meals.
candidates.why: Non-alcoholic option that the whole family can enjoy. The thyme-lemon combination echoes the Mediterranean and Middle Eastern flavors threading through the week. Spring-forward and celebratory.
